title: Canonical central p-torsion kernel and its wound criterion
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p$ prime [def-weil-field]. Groups are affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and smooth and connected mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ [def-sc-gm-ga] and $\mathbb A^1_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. A smooth connected unipotent $k$-group is called $k$-wound if every $k$-scheme morphism $\mathbb A^1_k\to H$ is constant with value in $H(k)$. Here unipotent means having a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation with unipotent geometric points [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]. The condition $[p]_H=0$ for a commutative group means that on every commutative $k$-algebra the sum of $p$ copies of each section is zero. Let $U$ be smooth, connected and unipotent. There is a largest smooth connected central subgroup $F\subseteq U$ with $[p]_F=0$: every smooth connected central subgroup killed by $p$ is contained in $F$. Centrality means that its sections commute with all sections of $U$ after every commutative algebra extension. This subgroup is commutative, is uniquely determined as a closed subgroup of $U$, and is called the cckp-kernel. Woundness and the cckp-kernel condition are the predicates of [def-sfb-wound-cckp-kernel]. Its formation commutes with every separable field extension $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: scalar extension is the pullback of [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], and $F_K$ is the cckp-kernel of $U_K$. Moreover $U$ is $k$-wound if and only if $F$ is $k$-wound. The trivial group $U=1$ is allowed, with $F=1$. No perfectness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Brian Conrad, The structure of solvable groups over general fields (2014), Definition 2.1, printed p.10; Definition 3.1 and the paragraph following it, printed p.15; Proposition 3.2, printed pp.15--16, equivalence (1) and (3). Read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf. WANTED locally: this document. No Stacks tag is claimed for this Tits structure theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change], $Z=Z(U)$ is a closed commutative affine finite-type group. Multiplication by $p$ is a homomorphism on $Z$ (commutativity lets one rearrange the $p$ factors). By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup] its kernel $H=\ker([p]_Z)$ is a closed subgroup. Apply [lem-sfb-separable-point-scheme-core] to $H$ and write $J=H^{\natural}$. Functoriality and compatibility with products restrict multiplication, inverse and identity to $J$, and its inclusion in $H$ is a homomorphism. The core is geometrically reduced, so [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] makes $J$ smooth. Its sections are central in $U$ and killed by $p$, because the same is true in $H$. In particular $J$ is commutative.

source.place: Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2, printed pp.15--16; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; agent assembly using the general separable-point core construction.

proof.text: Let $F=J^0$, the open and closed identity subgroup supplied by [lem-sfb-finite-type-group-identity-subgroup]. It is smooth by restriction of the smooth structure map of $J$, connected, central and killed by $p$. Let $B\subseteq U$ be any smooth connected central subgroup killed by $p$. It factors through $H$, by the stated universal descriptions of the centre and kernel. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], $B$ is geometrically reduced, so $B^{\natural}=B$ and core functoriality factors $B\to H$ through $J$. The image is connected and contains the identity, hence lies in the open and closed subscheme $J^0$ and factors through it. Thus $B\subseteq F$. This proves largestness, and two largest closed subgroups contain each other, so are equal. For $U=1$ the construction gives $H=J=F=1$.

source.place: Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2, printed pp.15--16; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; agent assembly using the general separable-point core construction.

proof.text: Let $K/k$ be separable. The centre commutes with scalar extension by [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change]. The $p$-fold multiplication map also commutes with it, and the defining fibre product of its kernel therefore gives $H_K=\ker([p]_{Z(U_K)})$. By [lem-sfb-separable-point-scheme-core], $J_K=(H_K)^{\natural}$. The subgroup $F_K$ is open and closed in $J_K$, contains the identity, and is connected: apply [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] to $F$, with its identity section. Consequently it is exactly the identity component of $J_K$: any connected subset containing the identity lies in this clopen subset, while $F_K$ itself is connected. The group $U_K$ is again smooth (base change of the smooth structure map, [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]), connected by [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] applied to $U$ with its identity section, and unipotent: base change of the closed immersion $U\to\mathcal U_n$ of [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding] is a faithful representation of $U_K$ by unitriangular matrices, so every geometric point of $U_K$ is unipotent. Steps 1--2 over $K$ now identify $F_K$ with the cckp-kernel of $U_K$. This uses the actual separable-core base-change assertion, not an assumption that reduction commutes with arbitrary field extension.

proof.text: If $U$ is $k$-wound, compose any morphism $\mathbb A^1_k\to F$ with the inclusion in $U$. Its composite is constant at its value at $0$. Since the inclusion is a monomorphism on all test schemes, the original morphism equals the constant morphism with that same $F(k)$-value. Hence $F$ is $k$-wound.

source.place: Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2, printed pp.15--16; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf; agent assembly using the general separable-point core construction.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $U$ is not $k$-wound. Choose a nonconstant $f:\mathbb A^1_k\to U$ and translate so $f(0)=1$. Extend to a separable closure $s=k_s$; nonconstancy persists since a nonconstant coordinate polynomial stays nonconstant under an injective field extension. By [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding] embed $U$ into $\mathcal U_n$ over $k$. Use the filtration $\mathcal U_n=U^{(0)}\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U^{(m)}=1$ of [lem-sfb-unitriangular-coordinate-filtration]. Its conjugation formula gives $[\mathcal U_n,U^{(r)}]\subseteq U^{(r+1)}$. If the current pointed nonconstant curve $a:\mathbb A^1_s\to U_s$ is not central, some $g\in U(s)$ does not commute with its image. Indeed the commutator $U_s\times\mathbb A^1_s\to U_s$ is then not identically $1$; write a nonzero pulled-back affine coordinate as a polynomial in the line variable with coefficients in $s[U]$. Smoothness makes $s[U]$ reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], and [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] ensures a nonzero coefficient is nonzero at some $g\in U(s)$. Replace $a(t)$ by $g^{-1}a(t)^{-1}ga(t)$. It is pointed and not identically $1$, hence nonconstant, and it moves one step deeper in the matrix filtration. After at most $m$ replacements a nonconstant curve must therefore be central; otherwise it would land in $U^{(m)}=1$. Denote the resulting central pointed curve by $c$.

tool_uses.why: Applied to the identity component with its rational identity to identify its base changes as identity components; no in-unit statement covers arbitrary ground fields.

Detect a nonzero commutator coefficient by a rational point over a separably closed field; the in-unit rational-point subspace test assumes an algebraically closed field and concerns linear representations.
Smooth subgroup and ambient group coordinate algebras are geometrically reduced; used for core functoriality and density detection, without any alternate unit route.
The scheme-theoretic fibre over the identity is a closed subgroup; the construction of the p-kernel needs this general group-scheme tool.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unipotent_cckpKernel_wound_criterion {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (U : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hU : SolvableGroupStructure.IsAlgebraic U) [Smooth U.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace U.X.left] (hunip : SolvableGroupStructure.IsUnipotent U) : ∃ (F : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (i : F ⟶ U), IsCckpKernel p i ∧ IsCommMonObj F.X ∧ (∀ (F' : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (i' : F' ⟶ U), IsCckpKernel p i' → ∃ e : F ≅ F', e.hom ≫ i' = i) ∧ (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hK : Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K), IsCckpKernel p ((MultiplicativeType.baseChange (K := K)).map i)) ∧ (IsWound U ↔ IsWound F)

statement_change.old_statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p$ prime [def-weil-field]. Groups are affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and smooth and connected mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ [def-sc-gm-ga] and $\mathbb A^1_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. A smooth connected unipotent $k$-group is called $k$-wound if every $k$-scheme morphism $\mathbb A^1_k\to H$ is constant with value in $H(k)$. Here unipotent means having a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation with unipotent geometric points. The condition $[p]_H=0$ for a commutative group means that on every commutative $k$-algebra the sum of $p$ copies of each section is zero. Let $U$ be smooth, connected and unipotent. There is a largest smooth connected central subgroup $F\subseteq U$ with $[p]_F=0$: every smooth connected central subgroup killed by $p$ is contained in $F$. Centrality means that its sections commute with all sections of $U$ after every commutative algebra extension. This subgroup is commutative, is uniquely determined as a closed subgroup of $U$, and is called the cckp-kernel. Its formation commutes with every separable field extension $K/k$: $F_K$ is the cckp-kernel of $U_K$. Moreover $U$ is $k$-wound if and only if $F$ is $k$-wound. The trivial group $U=1$ is allowed, with $F=1$. No perfectness hypothesis is imposed.
